text:
A: Hello! There we go. Can you hear me alright, mate?
B: Yeah, loud and clear. Hi, I'm Isaac.
A: Isaac, nice one. I'm Daniel. Right, first thing, I have to say it: I clocked the Barbican print in your photo. Great taste. Shame about the Palace scarf next to it.
B: Ha, I knew that was coming. I saw the West Ham mug though, so, you know, glass houses.
A: Fair, fair. We were a shambles at the weekend, honestly. I'm not even gonna defend it. So what do you do, Isaac? I had you down as a student, maybe?
B: Yeah, second year Economics at City. I commute in from Croydon.
A: Oh, brilliant. Economics. I teach, so I'm always nosy about what people end up doing. I'm Head of History at a big academy in north-east London, Walthamstow way. And what do you want to do with it? Let me guess, the City?
B: Erm, yeah, kind of, banking or consulting ideally. I'm applying for spring weeks at the moment. And I run a sort of tutoring thing on the side, maths and economics, GCSE and A-level.
A: Oh, do you? That's great, that's proper entrepreneurial. What did you get at A-level, if you don't mind me being a teacher about it?
B: Erm, A's, basically. Maths, Economics, and Philosophy. Philosophy was, like, borderline.
A: Philosophy, love that. See, I always say to my Year 13s, the ones who do a slightly unusual subject alongside, they interview better. They've got something to talk about, do you know what I mean? I'm doing a leadership qualification at the moment, NPQSL, the school's paying for it, and half of it's basically that. Can you hold a room, can you tell a story.
B: Yeah, that makes sense. Presenting's kind of the bit I actually like, to be fair. Seminars and that.
A: You'd be good at it, you've got the face for it. Sorry, that sounds weird. What I mean is you come across well. Very easy to talk to.
B: Ha, thanks, man. Erm, I saw the Lisbon print as well, behind you. Have you been?
A: Lisbon, yeah, twice. Oh, you'd love it. Honestly, for someone into buildings, it's unreal. The tiles, the azulejos, the whole of Alfama. We stayed in this hotel up the top, I paid for the upgrade, and the view over the river at sunset, I'm not exaggerating, people stop what they're doing. I sort of became the tour guide for everyone. My wife was like, Daniel, nobody asked about the earthquake of 1755.
B: Ha! Nah, I'd want to know about the earthquake, though. I'm saving for a trip, actually, Lisbon or Copenhagen, for the architecture.
A: Do Lisbon. Do Lisbon first. I'll give you my list, I've got a whole note on my phone. Restaurants, the lot.
B: That'd be sick, actually. Is it expensive?
A: Cheaper than London, put it that way. Most things are, innit.
B: Ha, true. Did you do the puzzle thing at the start? I was just saying to the last guy, I always get tense with timed stuff.
A: Oh, I smashed it. Well, I say smashed it. Got through all of them, couple I wasn't sure on. I captain a pub quiz team, so I'm used to the clock. We came second again last week, robbed on the music round, honestly robbed.
B: Second's still good, though.
A: Second's the first loser, mate. That's what I tell my department.
B: Ha. Bit harsh.
A: I'm joking. Mostly. Who'd you have before me, then?
B: Haider, the IT guy. He was really chill. Chelsea fan, though.
A: Ah, I'm on with him later, I think. Right, so tell me about the tutoring, how many students have you got—
